userStories.title: Token-2022 extensions
userStories.description: As a user, I want examples using Token-2022 program features.
acceptanceCriteria: Features: transfer fees or interest-bearing or metadata pointer
Tests verify extension data is set correctly
userStories.notes: Seahorse at examples/token_2022.py. Reference at tests/anchor-reference/token_2022_anchor/. NOTE: Seahorse doesn't have native Token-2022 support (only legacy SPL Token via TokenMint/TokenAccount). The Seahorse example demonstrates fee configuration tracking with FeeConfig PDA storing mint, authority, decimals, transfer_fee_bps, max_fee, and total_fees_collected. Instructions: initialize_fee_config, update_fee_rate, calculate_transfer_fee, record_fee_collection, get_fee_info. The Anchor reference implements actual Token-2022 transfer fee extension using spl-token-2022 crate with manual CPI for mint initialization and fee withdrawal. 17 LiteSVM integration tests covering fee config initialization, fee rate updates, fee calculation (including max fee capping), fee recording, and authorization checks. Parity is conceptual - both programs track transfer fees but Anchor interacts with Token-2022 while Seahorse tracks configuration only.

userStories.title: Escrow program - Seahorse implementation
userStories.description: As a user, I want a Seahorse escrow program for trustless token swaps.
acceptanceCriteria: Find reference Anchor escrow from solana-developers/program-examples or anchor-escrow-2025
userStories.notes: Seahorse at examples/escrow.py. Reference at tests/anchor-reference/escrow_anchor/. Instructions: make_escrow (maker deposits Token A, specifies Token B wanted), take_escrow (taker sends Token B, receives Token A), cancel_escrow (maker recovers Token A). PDA seeds use escrow_id only (not maker + escrow_id) to work around Seahorse limitation with UncheckedAccount in signer seeds. Escrow PDA is vault authority. Vault derived with seeds=['vault', escrow_id].

userStories.title: Escrow program - tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I need comprehensive tests for the escrow program.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests for full happy path (init -> accept)
Tests for failure cases (wrong amounts, wrong parties)
Behavior parity verified against Anchor reference
userStories.notes: 11 LiteSVM integration tests (tests/integration/escrow_integration.rs): make_escrow (single, multiple, zero amount errors), take_escrow (happy path, wrong maker, insufficient funds), cancel_escrow (happy path, unauthorized), full workflow tests. 4 Seahorse behavior tests (tests/common/escrow_parity.rs): state initialization, full workflow, cancel, deterministic PDA. Note: Seahorse and Anchor escrow have different account interfaces (Seahorse uses basic token accounts, Anchor uses ATA constraints and InterfaceAccount types) so true parity tests were replaced with independent behavior verification. Fixed escrow.py program ID (was invalid 43-char base58) and compiled escrow.rs bug (escrow.escrow_id -> escrow.borrow().escrow_id in PDA signer seeds).

userStories.title: Token swap AMM - Seahorse implementation
userStories.description: As a user, I want a basic AMM/swap example demonstrating liquidity pool mechanics.
userStories.notes: Seahorse at examples/token_swap.py. Reference at tests/anchor-reference/token_swap_anchor/. Pool PDA with seeds=['pool', mint_a, mint_b]. Instructions: initialize_pool (creates pool, LP mint, pool token accounts), add_liquidity (geometric mean for first deposit, proportional for subsequent), remove_liquidity (burn LP, receive proportional tokens), swap (constant product formula with configurable fee). Minimum liquidity (100) locked on first deposit. Slippage protection via min_lp_tokens and min_amount_out. isqrt function implements integer square root using Newton's method.

userStories.title: Token swap AMM - tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I need comprehensive tests for the AMM program.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests verify swap math is correct
Behavior parity verified against Anchor reference
userStories.notes: 20 LiteSVM integration tests (tests/integration/token_swap_integration.rs): pool initialization (basic, different fees, invalid fee), add liquidity (first deposit, subsequent, imbalanced, slippage, zero amount, too small), remove liquidity (partial, full, slippage, zero amount), swap (A to B, B to A, different fees, slippage, zero amount), full workflow, constant product invariant. 5 parity tests (tests/common/token_swap_parity.rs): pool initialization state, first deposit LP formula (sqrt(a*b) - 100), swap math constant product formula with fees, LP token accounting, deterministic PDA derivation. Swap math verified: output = (amount_in * (10000 - fee_bps) * reserve_out) / (reserve_in * 10000 + amount_in * (10000 - fee_bps)).

userStories.title: Staking program

acceptanceCriteria: Tests use LiteSVM time warping for reward accumulation
userStories.notes: 7 LiteSVM integration tests (tests/integration/staking_integration.rs): initialize_pool, stake, unstake_with_rewards (uses warp_to_slot), claim_rewards_without_unstaking, error cases (zero amount, unstake more than staked, claim with no stake). 5 parity tests (tests/common/staking_parity.rs): pool initialization state, stake updates pool totals, reward calculation formula (staked_amount * reward_rate * slots_elapsed / REWARD_SCALE), claim_rewards preserves stake, deterministic PDA derivation. Reward formula verified with time warping.

userStories.title: Lending pool (deposit/borrow)
userStories.description: As a user, I want a simplified lending example demonstrating collateralization.
userStories.notes: Seahorse at examples/lending.py. Reference at tests/anchor-reference/lending_anchor/. Implements simplified lending protocol: deposit_collateral (secure borrowing position), borrow (against collateral at 150% ratio), repay (with interest), withdraw_collateral (if ratio maintained). Interest calculated per slot: borrowed * rate * slots / INTEREST_SCALE. Pool PDA uses collateral_mint only. 13 LiteSVM integration tests: pool initialization, deposit/withdraw collateral, borrow within/exceeds ratio, repay partial/full, withdraw with/without debt, interest accrual, error cases (zero amount, insufficient liquidity), full workflow. 5 parity tests: pool initialization state, collateral ratio enforcement (150% = 15000 BPS), interest accrual formula, full lending workflow, deterministic PDA derivation.

userStories.title: Vesting schedule
userStories.description: As a user, I want a token vesting example with cliff and linear release.
acceptanceCriteria: Cliff period, linear vesting after cliff
Tests verify partial claims work correctly
userStories.notes: Seahorse at examples/vesting.py. Reference at tests/anchor-reference/vesting_anchor/. VestingAccount stores: authority, beneficiary, mint, vault, total_amount, released_amount, start_slot, cliff_slot, end_slot, is_cancelled, bump. Instructions: create_vesting (with cliff_slots + vesting_duration_slots), claim_vested (linear release after cliff), cancel_vesting (authority returns unvested, beneficiary gets vested). Linear vesting formula: vested = total * (current_slot - cliff_slot) / (end_slot - cliff_slot). 14 LiteSVM integration tests: create with/without cliff, claim before/at/after cliff, partial claims, authorization, cancel at various points, full workflow. 5 parity tests: initialization state, cliff enforcement, linear vesting calculation, partial claims work correctly, deterministic PDA derivation. All tests use warp_to_slot() for time-based testing.

userStories.title: Auction program
userStories.description: As a user, I want an auction example demonstrating time-based state transitions.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests use LiteSVM time warping for auction end
userStories.notes: Seahorse at examples/auction.py. Reference at tests/anchor-reference/auction_anchor/. Token-based auction (not SOL) because Seahorse doesn't support PDA-signed lamport transfers - only TokenAccount.transfer() with signer seeds. Auction account: seller, auction_id, bid_mint, starting_price, current_bid, highest_bidder, start_slot, end_slot, is_ended, is_claimed, bump. Instructions: create_auction (creates auction PDA and bid escrow vault), place_bid (outbids previous, refunds previous bidder via PDA-signed transfer), end_auction (marks ended after end_slot), claim_prize (winner confirms, seller receives payment). 16 LiteSVM integration tests covering all instructions, validation failures, time warping. 6 parity tests verifying state initialization, bid refund mechanics, time enforcement, PDA derivation.

userStories.title: NFT minting with Metaplex
userStories.description: As a user, I want an NFT minting example using Metaplex Token Metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: Find reference Anchor NFT minting program with Metaplex
CPI to Metaplex Token Metadata program
Create metadata, mint NFT, set URI
Tests verify metadata account created correctly
userStories.notes: Seahorse at examples/nft_mint.py. Reference at tests/anchor-reference/nft_mint_anchor/. NOTE: Seahorse doesn't have native Metaplex Token Metadata support (no CPI wrappers for mpl-token-metadata). The Seahorse example demonstrates NFT configuration tracking with NftConfig PDA storing: authority, nft_id, mint, name (max 32 chars), symbol (max 10 chars), uri (max 200 chars), is_minted, bump. Instructions: create_nft_config (validate lengths, init PDA), update_nft_config (update before minting), mark_as_minted (record mint address, set flag), get_nft_info (log config). The Anchor reference implements full Metaplex CPI for mint_nft (creates mint, metadata account, master edition) plus parity-compatible instructions (create_nft_config, update_nft_config, mark_as_minted). 13 LiteSVM integration tests: create config (basic, different IDs, name/symbol too long), update config (basic, unauthorized, after minting fails), mark_as_minted (basic, unauthorized, twice fails), get_nft_info, full workflow, PDA determinism. Parity is conceptual - Anchor does actual Metaplex CPI while Seahorse tracks configuration only.
